text: King Dasaratha and Queen Kausalya welcome Rama at dawn.
Rama is born with divine attributes: lotus-red eyes, lengthy arms, roseate lips, and a voice like drumbeat.
Sage Viswamitra arrives in Ayodhya seeking help against evil forces.
Dasaratha promises to place his trust in Rama's path.
Rama expresses his desire to serve justice and protect the innocent.
Rama and Viswamitra form a mentor-protégé relationship.
Rama and his brother agree to fight for justice together in Dandakaranya.
Rama and Lakshmana enter the Dandakaranya forest under Viswamitra's guidance.
Tadaka, a yaksha woman turned rakshasi, confronts Rama and Lakshmana in the misty forest.
Rama refuses to judge Tadaka by gender and challenges her for her deeds.
Lakshmana stands up to Tadaka, showing his loyalty and courage.
Rama defeats Tadaka with a single arrow, breaking her curse and ending her dark power.
Viswamitra gives Rama a divine weapon, an astra, to protect the innocent.
Lakshmana receives a sacred sword, a sastra, from Viswamitra.
Rama vows to use his divine weapons only to defend the innocent.
Rama accepts the divine bow Shiv Dhanush from King Janaka.
Rama breaks the Shiv Dhanush in two to demonstrate his strength and humility.
Sita expresses her admiration for Rama's divine power.
King Janaka announces Sita's hand in marriage to the worthy soul.
Rama accepts Sita's hand in marriage, vowing to protect her and Ayodhya.
Lakshmana pledges his loyalty to Rama and vows to protect their homeland.
Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita approach Ayodhya's gates under cover of night.
Shiv Dhanush is a divine bow crafted by Lord Shiva himself.
Kaikeyi demands that Rama be exiled and Bharata made king.
Dasaratha is deeply sorrowful after granting Kaikeyi's wish.
Rama is set to leave Ayodhya, beginning his exile.
Kaikeyi and Dasaratha's relationship becomes strained as she pushes for her demand.
Rama vows to return to Ayodhya when the time is right.
Kaikeyi's true motives remain hidden, as she may have ulterior intentions.
